title: A Demonstration of Correlation Analysis in Python & Quarto
text:
Introduction

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

Does the width of the petal correlate with the length of the petal?
The students of UW-Madison DSHB program is interested in learning about the correlations between flower petal width and length. This program will use this topic as a demonstration of working with correlation analysis in Python and Quarto; we have
150 flowers.


Literature Review
{{lipsum>}}


Method
Given that we have two columns of continuous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters. We will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points when evaluating data like these


Results

corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

if corr_val > 0.8: 
    narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
    narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -0.4:
    narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"

Using the class simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of 0.96287. We conclude the relation is a very strong positive correlation.

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6,3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Petal Length (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal Width (mm)')







Figure 1: A scatterplot of petal length and width





As shown in @gif-length-width-scatter we see additional evidence of a strong positive correlation between an iris flower petal length and width


Discussion
Now that this long-standing problem is resolved (thanks to the diligent efforts of UW-Madison’s DSHB program), they have once again triumphed in establishing that there is a positive correlative relationship between iris petal length and petal width as a matter of empirically certain ground truth.
